headline: Evaluation protocols test whether single-cell and structure predictors hold up
label: Evaluating Computational Biology Models
summary: Recent preprints propose robustness benchmarks and evaluation taxonomies for single-cell and biomolecular predictors, alongside scalable tooling.
synthesis: The dominant thread is evaluation of computational predictors in single-cell and molecular biology, and what their outputs can support. FERRET benchmarks single-cell GRN inference by comparing within- and between-cell-type network robustness (RAUC, Monotonicity), validated with ChIP-seq. A separate preprint proposes a taxonomy of evaluation protocols for single-cell perturbation prediction models and releases scPertEval to assess those protocols. A perspective on AI biomolecular structure predictors reports persistent limitations, and explicit K+ ion addition shifts IDR and G-quadruplex conformations. HydrAffinity, an interaction-free mixture-of-experts affinity model, is primarily a modeling study at the edge of this thread. metaSMASH, NEXCISION, and Spectronaut-nf address scale and reproducibility of tooling. The new element is the protocol-level framing of evaluation, rather than single-benchmark reporting.
